searchText: Yea, somewhat like the BTC forks. But unlike the BTC forks we could theoretically build bridges for assets between these "forks"....right? Yeah you could but there would still be two copies of all of the assets on both ledgers and in the process double the market caps in a perfect world everyone would just cut the prices of everything exactly in half but that's not how things would shake out in practice (as, for example, the new circulating supply driving market prices down should immediately liquidate every makerdao vault at less than 200% collateralization) Is there a way to invalidate all the existing state of the chain? what about all existing state except eth holdings? I guess the first one could just be start from a genesis block, but what about the second There's not really a way to do that cleanly, what about eth in contract accounts? what about just eth that is staked What about it? Curious if/when core devs plan to address the issue where more than half of the nodes are still on the split chain. I know the key players like miners/exchanges have moved over but there's still 5000+ nodes that never came back there's not really anything they *can* do, anyone mining on that chain is doing so out of ignorance probably should ask in a remix-specific setting ¯\\_(ツ)\_/¯ I wouldn’t trust the numbers you get from crawlers. They’re notoriously inaccurate. Any node that’s still on the old chain is unused. If it was used the owner would have noticed no blocks coming in by now. Using etherscan's node tracker https://etherscan.io/nodetracker Done Np mate
